title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
description: Ten documented CSUN rituals and recurring campus celebrations, from roses at the Matador statue to the president’s commencement sneakers.

cards.title: Leave a Rose for the Matador
cards.subtitle: A red rose marks a new beginning, milestone or hard-won achievement
cards.notes: Bring a red rose to the Matador statue when starting at CSUN or celebrating a meaningful academic or personal milestone.
cards.short_summary: CSUN community members commemorate beginnings and achievements by placing red roses at the bronze Matador statue.
cards.evidence_claim: CSUN reports that students and alumni place red roses at the Matador statue for milestones, and that Associated Students formally introduced the practice in 2011.
cards.source_title: Did You Know? CSUN’s Tradition of the Rose
cards.access_notes: The statue is on Matador Walk between the University Library and University Student Union; campus access rules apply.

cards.title: Enter the Powwow Circle Respectfully
cards.subtitle: A four-decade pan-tribal gathering rooted in CSUN’s American Indian community
cards.notes: Watch the Grand Entry and cultural presentations with respect; follow announcements and ask before photographing participants.
cards.short_summary: The annual campus gathering brings Indigenous dance, song, ceremony and community education to Sierra Quad.
cards.evidence_claim: CSUN documented its 40th annual Powwow in 2025 and identifies it as a tradition created by the American Indian Student Association and American Indian Studies Program.
cards.source_title: CSUN’s Annual Powwow Celebrates 40 Years of Bringing Together SoCal American Indian Communities
cards.access_notes: The documented 2025 gathering was free and open to the public at Sierra Quad; consult the next event notice before attending.

cards.title: Meet the Library Lawn’s Giant Concert
cards.subtitle: Associated Students turns a central campus lawn into an annual music event
cards.notes: Check the current Big Show announcement for admission rules, then arrive through the designated student-entry checkpoint.
cards.short_summary: Big Show is CSUN Associated Students’ recurring large-scale concert on the University Library Lawn.
cards.evidence_claim: CSUN’s newsroom describes Big Show as an annual Associated Students music event and documented its return to the University Library Lawn in October 2025.
cards.source_title: Fall(ing) for Big Show, with Galantis
cards.access_notes: Attendance conditions and timing vary by edition; verify the current Associated Students event announcement before going.

cards.title: Start Fall Under the Neon Lights
cards.subtitle: A student-only carnival-and-dance-night tradition at the University Student Union
cards.notes: Bring a valid CSUN student ID, review the current entry policy and explore the event’s rides, games and photo areas.
cards.short_summary: Matador Nights opens the academic year with a changing mix of carnival attractions, music and campus activities.
cards.evidence_claim: CSUN Magazine calls Matador Nights a beloved annual campus tradition and documented the student-only September 2025 edition.
cards.access_notes: This is a CSUN-students-only event; the 2025 edition occurred at the University Student Union, and future details may change.

cards.title: Process onto the Library Lawn
cards.subtitle: CSUN’s entering class receives its formal welcome each fall
cards.notes: New students should RSVP when registration opens, meet at Matador Walk and follow staff into the lawn ceremony.
cards.short_summary: The annual convocation marks the academic year’s opening with university welcomes, music and a rose ceremony.
cards.evidence_claim: CSUN states that New Student Convocation has been an annual celebration since 2007 and marks the official start of the academic year for new students.
cards.access_notes: The 2026 event is scheduled for September 24; participation information and RSVP access are intended for new CSUN students.

cards.entity_name: CSUN Alma Mater at New Student Convocation
cards.title: Sing “Hail to the Matadors”
cards.subtitle: The entering class closes its formal welcome with CSUN’s school song
cards.notes: Follow the student-government song leader during convocation and join the Alma Mater before the rose ceremony begins.
cards.short_summary: New Matadors sing the university Alma Mater together as part of the annual convocation program.
cards.evidence_claim: CSUN’s published New Student Convocation timeline places the Alma Mater after the Associated Students president’s greeting and before concluding remarks and the Rose Ceremony.
cards.access_notes: This ritual occurs within New Student Convocation, whose participation information is directed to incoming CSUN students.

cards.title: Celebrate Black Matador Legacy
cards.subtitle: A time-honored ceremony centered on Black academic achievement
cards.notes: Eligible graduates should complete the official application, obtain required tickets and monitor the page for ceremony updates.
cards.short_summary: Black Graduation brings graduates, families and the campus community together in an affirming commencement celebration.
cards.evidence_claim: CSUN’s official page documents the 2026 Black Graduation ceremony, while its newsroom describes the event as a time-honored CSUN tradition.
cards.source_title: First Gen and Future Leaders: CSUN Commencement 2025
cards.access_notes: Graduate participation requires an application and tickets; follow the official Black Graduation page for each year’s requirements.

cards.title: Cross the Stage for a Rainbow Sash
cards.subtitle: CSUN honors queer graduates with a dedicated community ceremony
cards.notes: Graduates should RSVP through the official event page and invite supporters to the staged sash presentation and program.
cards.short_summary: Rainbow Graduation recognizes queer achievement through student performances, speakers and a rainbow-sash presentation.
cards.evidence_claim: CSUN’s official 2026 event page invited graduates to walk across the stage and receive a rainbow sash during Rainbow Graduation at the University Student Union.
cards.access_notes: The documented 2026 ceremony required an RSVP and welcomed graduates’ friends and family; future arrangements may differ.

cards.title: Receive the Honors Medallion in Your Seat
cards.subtitle: CSUN separates scholastic recognition from the main commencement ceremonies
cards.notes: Invited graduates should RSVP in Tassel, claim guest tickets and follow instructions for receiving the honors medallion.
cards.short_summary: The annual lawn ceremony recognizes qualifying graduates with medallions before CSUN’s commencement exercises.
cards.evidence_claim: CSUN’s 2026 invitation identifies Honors Convocation as an annual ceremony and states that graduates receive their medallions while seated.
cards.source_title: Honors Convocation Ceremony RSVP & Tickets (Scholastic Achievement)
cards.access_notes: Participation is by nomination and requires an RSVP; invited graduates may claim up to four guest tickets under the 2026 instructions.

cards.title: Spot the Sparkly Red Sneakers
cards.subtitle: CSUN’s president pairs academic regalia with bright red Converse at commencement
cards.notes: Look toward the commencement platform during the presidential welcome to spot the red sneakers beneath the formal regalia.
cards.short_summary: President Erika D. Beck’s sparkly red “Commencement Chucks” add a recurring personal custom to CSUN graduation.
cards.evidence_claim: CSUN’s 2026 commencement recap states that President Erika D. Beck customarily welcomes graduates while wearing sparkly red Converse sneakers with her academic regalia.
cards.source_title: Families, Friends and Matador Pride Fill Campus for Commencement 2026
cards.access_notes: Visible during CSUN commencement ceremonies; ceremony admission and ticket requirements apply to graduates and guests.
